sections.html:
Wayne County is in east central Indiana on the Ohio border. Richmond is the county seat and largest city, and smaller communities include Centerville, Cambridge City, Hagerstown, Dalton, Pennville and Fountain City. The county covers about 404 square miles.

The population is 66,169 as of July 2025, down 0.6% from the 2020 base and down from 68,917 in 2010. The county has 30,804 housing units and 26,975 households. Owners occupy 69.2% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $140,200, median gross rent is $815 and median household income is $55,692. Building permits totaled 271 in 2025.

Richmond has several historic districts, and older houses in them often need more upkeep than newer ones. Roofs, furnaces and foundations take the brunt of Indiana's temperature swings, and repair needs are a common reason owners consider selling as-is.

The Wayne County Assessor values each parcel. The office is on the lower level of the Wayne County Administration Building at 301 E. Main St. in Richmond. You can look up the assessed value of any parcel on Beacon, the Schneider online records site.

If you disagree with a value, Indiana's general appeal rule uses Form 130:

  • File by June 15 of the year that matches your notice. In 2025 the Wayne deadline was June 16, so confirm the date printed on your notice.
  • File one petition per parcel.
  • The PTABOA must hold a hearing within 180 days.
  • Appeal a PTABOA decision to the Indiana Board of Tax Review with Form 131.

The average Wayne County assessment rose 15% in 2025. The assessor explained that the state raised its cost tables 30 to 35% across the board because of labor and material costs, and that 2024 assessments for sold properties averaged about 78% of sale prices.

Form 11 notices had to be mailed by April 30. Owners could scan the QR code on the notice to appeal online, download Form 130 or go to the assessor's office. An appeal brings an individual review of the property rather than the mass assessment.

If you received a large increase, keep that notice. A higher assessment can carry over into a buyer's costs, and an appeal still open at closing is worth mentioning to the title company.

Wayne County property tax is due in two installments, May 11 and November 10 in 2026. The treasurer mails one bill a year by April 15 with both coupons. Penalties begin the day after each due date, and partial payments are accepted any time, though the full amount is due by the deadline.

The 10% rate applies from the start, instead of 5%, if the owner has prior delinquent taxes.

sections.h2: What an appeal looks like in practice
sections.html:
1. Read the Form 11 notice when it arrives, and compare the description of the house with the real one: square footage, finished space, condition.
  2. Decide how to file: scan the QR code on the notice, download Form 130, or take it to the assessor's office.
  3. Gather support, such as a recent sale of a similar house, a repair estimate or photos of damage.
  4. The assessor reviews the individual property, and if you are not satisfied, the PTABOA holds a hearing within 180 days.
  5. A PTABOA decision can be taken to the Indiana Board of Tax Review with Form 131.

Remember that an appeal changes the assessment, not the rates set by local governments. Even a successful appeal may leave the bill higher than the year before if the county rose sharply.

The Treasurer's office is at 401 East Main Street, second floor of the Wayne County Annex, phone (765) 973-9238. Hours are Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30.

  • Online at taxes.quickviewhere.com, using the access code on your bill. Online balances leave out penalties, so call for the amount owed after the due date.
  • By phone at 1-877-690-3729, jurisdiction code 2412. Card fees apply.
  • By mail or in the drop box at the Annex. Do not put cash in the box.
  • In person at participating banks in the weeks before the spring due date, for a fee of $1 or $2 per parcel depending on the bank.

A house with delinquent tax can still be sold, because the title company pays the balance from your proceeds. Tax sale information for Wayne County runs through sriservices.com, and questions about redeeming a parcel after a sale go to the County Auditor.

Before you sell, call the treasurer for the exact amount including penalties, since the online balance leaves them out. Then compare that number with the price you expect to net.

We buy houses in Wayne County as-is, including ones with back taxes, repairs or tenants. The offer is ours to make and yours to decline, and nothing is owed if you say no.

Nothing about the county's rules blocks a sale. On closing day the title company contacts the treasurer to confirm the amount due, deducts it from your proceeds along with any mortgage payoff, and records the deed. A cash sale skips the buyer's lender, so there is no appraisal or loan approval to wait on, and the date depends mainly on the title work.

If a spring or fall installment has come due but has not been paid, the penalty clock is already running. Tell the buyer and the title company about it at the start, because the 5% and 10% penalties add to the payoff and the online balance will not show them.

sections.h2: What to do with a sale in mind
sections.html:
Start with three calls. The Assessor's office can confirm your parcel's assessed value and whether an appeal is possible. The Treasurer can give an exact payoff including penalties. The Auditor can answer questions about any tax sale involving the parcel.

  1. Pull your most recent Form 11 notice and tax bill.
  2. Write down the payoff amount and the date you were quoted it.
  3. Tell the title company about any appeal that is still open.
  4. Decide whether you would rather list the house or accept a direct offer, using the net amount after taxes and repairs.

Most sellers find that the tax piece is simpler than expected. Whatever is owed comes out of the proceeds, and the title company confirms the figure with the county before it prepares your closing statement.

faqs.q: When are Wayne County, Indiana property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments, due May 11 and November 10 in 2026. The treasurer mails one bill by April 15 that has both coupons.

faqs.q: What are the late penalties in Wayne County?
faqs.a: The penalty is 5% from the day after the due date and 10% after about 30 days. It is 10% from the start if you have prior delinquent taxes.

faqs.q: Where is the Wayne County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The office is at 401 East Main Street in Richmond, on the second floor of the Annex Building. The phone is (765) 973-9238.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Wayne County assessment?
faqs.a: File Indiana Form 130 with the Assessor, one per parcel, by June 15 of the right year.

faqs.q: Can I check my Wayne County assessed value online?
faqs.a: Yes. The Beacon site, run by Schneider, lets owners look up assessed values.
